competencies.name: Functions and functional zones
competencies.can: State the functions of the respiratory system and distinguish the conducting zone from the respiratory zone by structure and by role in gas exchange.

competencies.name: Pressure gradients and airflow
competencies.can: Apply Boyle's law to inspiration and expiration and relate alveolar pressure to atmospheric pressure at each point in a quiet breath.

competencies.name: Intrapleural pressure
competencies.can: Explain why intrapleural pressure is subatmospheric and predict what happens to the lung and chest wall when the pleural seal is broken.

competencies.name: Compliance and elastic recoil
competencies.can: Define lung compliance and elastic recoil and predict the effect of fibrosis and of emphysema on each.

competencies.name: Surfactant and surface tension
competencies.can: Explain how surfactant lowers surface tension and why its absence causes alveolar collapse in the premature newborn.

competencies.name: Airway resistance
competencies.can: Identify the main determinant of airway resistance and predict the effect of bronchoconstriction, mucus, and sympathetic stimulation on airflow.

competencies.name: Lung volumes and capacities
competencies.can: Define tidal volume, inspiratory and expiratory reserve volume, residual volume, vital capacity, and total lung capacity and read each from a spirogram.

competencies.name: Obstructive and restrictive patterns
competencies.can: Use the ratio of forced expiratory volume in one second to forced vital capacity to classify a spirometry result as obstructive or restrictive.

competencies.name: Alveolar ventilation and dead space
competencies.can: Calculate minute ventilation and alveolar ventilation and explain why slow deep breathing ventilates the alveoli better than rapid shallow breathing.

competencies.name: Spirometry
competencies.can: Record a spirogram, calculate the lung volumes and capacities available from it, and compare the results with predicted values.
